markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Training margins depend on negative sampling and score scale. They do not establish validation ranking quality. (2) Feedback suggests insufficient attention to recent, repeated interests. Their correlation requires controls before attributing sensitivity to either. (3) Descriptions can support compatibility checks. Missing specifications remain unknown; interactions establish neither ownership nor satisfied demand.

**Related-work insights.** (1) Oh and Cho [1] measure last-item repetition. Their filtering improvements offer limited guidance when evaluation excludes seen items. (2) Counterfactual recommendation studies [2] motivate history interventions. Conditional permutation [4] motivates matching correlated signals, an adaptation rather than an established sequential-recommendation protocol. (3) Sampled-evaluation research [3] motivates supplementary full-catalog checks. Perturbation-faithfulness research [5] cautions that distribution shift can mimic importance.

These insights define three directions: controlled history dependence, adaptive temporal weighting, and evidence-supported semantic precision.

### Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Interpretive limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| History dependence | Training prefixes | Matched deletion; supported masking | Sensitivity is model dependence |
| Temporal weighting | Positions; timestamps | Learned recency gate | Recent need not mean relevant |
| Semantic precision | Titles; descriptions | Explicit specification checks | Missing evidence remains unknown |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Controlled history-dependence probe [2,4,5]: 5/6/5.** Originality: useful controlled adaptation, but established ingredients. Potential: actionable hypotheses, but no demonstrated HR benefit. Difficulty: existing hooks help, but matching and attention semantics require care.
2. **Gated recent-history residual [1]: 4/7/5.** Mix SASRec features with recent-item pooling. Originality: adaptive combination, but familiar components. Potential: directly tests ranking improvement, but can amplify incidental interests. Difficulty: compact change, but requires retraining and predictor updates.
3. **Specification-supported mismatch audit: 6/6/6.** Extract explicit model/interface tokens. Originality: evidence-specific matching, but familiar extraction rules. Potential: interpretable cases, but sparse metadata limits coverage. Difficulty: simple matching, but reliable contradictions are harder.

### Selected idea: controlled history-dependence probe

At 0% progress, retain this as a bounded diagnostic experiment; its cost-effectiveness is unproven. Reserve an equal GPU-time comparison for the gated residual, with trial counts and diagnostic-to-change rules fixed beforehand.

Use fixed training prefixes. Separate recent-only, recurrent-only, overlapping, and neither positions. Define recurrence from repeated IDs or a frozen lexical rule. Compare equal-count deletions matched on position, elapsed time, training popularity, and final-item treatment; report unmatched coverage. Recency contrasts cannot match away recency itself.

Keep candidates and original eligibility masks fixed. Measure top-10 overlap, original-top-item rank displacement, and paired ranking changes against repeated controls. Report compact deletion separately from architecture-supported fixed-slot masking; shuffle nonpadding tokens with a last-item-fixed control. Verify positions, attention exclusions, and readout. Perturbations remain potentially out of distribution.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, actual `view.model`, mode restoration, and metrics/definitions. Stratify by dataset/history length; bootstrap users. Select changes only with pinned macro validation HR@10; log runtime and every trial. Twenty qualitative users support cases, not population claims.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606), [3](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2491635/), [5](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/file/fe4b8556000d0f0cae99daa5c5c5a410-Paper.pdf).

idea.description: Strengthen the diagnostic adapter with bounded, conditionally matched history perturbations, and test whether its predefined recommendations provide useful guidance relative to a budget-matched gated recent-history baseline.
idea.motivation: Existing probes measure embedding geometry and sampled training-pair separation. History interventions can investigate the qualitative complaint about broad relatedness, but recency, recurrence, popularity, positional changes, and unfamiliar inputs can confound interpretation. Diagnostic sensitivity and diagnostic cost-effectiveness therefore require separate evaluation; neither establishes user intent or guarantees HR@10 improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Use view.model as the trained module and restore its original training mode in finally. Preserve existing embedding and margin probes; label their score-scale and sampled-negative limitations. Leave unavailable category breakdowns empty with an explicit unavailable reason. Do not use ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, inferred ownership, or simulator traits.

Freeze the protocol before observing perturbation results. Per dataset, select up to 32 eligible training users using seed 42, and use their complete observed training histories truncated to the model's existing maximum length. Exclude held-out validation/test events and do not reconstruct prefixes from right-shifted loader targets. Require at least eight nonpadding interactions. Define recent positions as the last ceil(0.25*n) interactions. Define recurrent interest through repeated IDs or title/description TF-IDF cosine similarity >=0.5 to another observed prefix item, using a vocabulary fitted only on metadata for training-observed items. Freeze tokenization, vocabulary, threshold, and preprocessing; missing text supplies no lexical match. Record ID-based and lexical coverage separately. Similarity is an operational grouping rule, not established shared intent.

Partition positions into recent-only, recurrent-only, overlapping, and neither. For each eligible group choose k=min(2, group size), retaining at least two interactions. For recurrence contrasts, sample five equal-count controls without replacement within each draw from nonrecurrent positions matched on relative-position quartile, elapsed-time bin, training-frequency quartile, and final-item status. Use elapsed-time bins <=7 days, >7 to 30 days, >30 to 180 days, and >180 days relative to the prefix endpoint; missing timestamps form a separate stratum. Count item frequency from training interactions only, and save bin edges. Require exact stratum-count matches; skip infeasible contrasts and report coverage rather than silently relaxing matching. Recent-only contrasts use equal-count nonrecent controls matched on popularity and recurrence status; position/time differences define that contrast and remain inseparable from it. Treat overlapping-group contrasts as joint sensitivity, not isolated recurrence effects. An isolated-interest contrast uses nonrecurrent positions outside the recent group with controls matched on position/time/popularity where feasible; report unavailable when the partition leaves no valid comparator. Fine strata may make these analyses sparse.

For the primary diagnostic, use one fixed full-catalog candidate set per user excluding all items in the original observed training history. Keep that set unchanged after interventions so removed items never become eligible. Do not add validation/test labels to eligibility decisions. Cache baseline scores and use chunked scoring with deterministic item-ID tie breaking. Report top-10 overlap as intersection size divided by 10, displacement as perturbed rank minus baseline rank of the original top item, and the original top-versus-runner-up score gap evaluated on those same two items. Score-gap changes remain scale dependent. Subtract the mean matched-control change from each targeted change; aggregate first within user, then within dataset. Bootstrap users within datasets for descriptive intervals, keeping all controls for a user together. These intervals do not quantify training-seed variation or prove causal preference.

Compact deletion follows the baseline's left-padding convention. Fixed-slot masking is available only after checking the actual architecture's position IDs, attention key exclusions, zero-query behavior, and final readout. Never assume an internal zero excludes an attention key. If masking requires changing the trained architecture's attention semantics, report it unavailable rather than presenting it as an equivalent intervention. Final-position masking needs a separately defined readout and must be reported separately or omitted. Shuffle only nonpadding history and include a last-item-fixed permutation control. Check shapes, finite outputs, baseline identity, deterministic ties, position assignments, and mode restoration. Positive score rescaling should preserve rank diagnostics while changing margins. Under independent continuous random scores, expected pinned HR@10 is 0.10 for 100 candidates; finite realizations fluctuate.

Predeclare a maximum diagnostic allocation of 5% of the remaining shared GPU-second budget, with measured runtime included. A predefined decision rule may nominate the gated residual only if the recurrence contrast has positive mean excess top-10 disruption in at least three datasets and adequate matched coverage, defined beforehand as at least 16 of the 32 sampled users per qualifying dataset. This is a heuristic nomination threshold, not a significance claim. Insufficient coverage produces an inconclusive diagnosis. The nominated change is tested once; it is never applied automatically. Run one equal-GPU-time direct gated-residual comparator regardless of probe outcome, reuse the same trained baseline, and log all costs and trials. This small comparison is exploratory evidence about utility, not a controlled general demonstration that diagnostics improve search.

For the comparator, mix the baseline final feature h with a projected mean of the last five nonpadding item embeddings: h_mix=(1-g)*h+g*W*pool, with scalar g=sigmoid(b), initialized to 0.1. Retain baseline item scoring, loss, optimizer, and training settings to isolate this change. Update the predictor writer and working/predict.py together if this model is trained. Select checkpoints and trials exclusively through the pinned four-dataset macro validation HR@10. If per-user outcomes are available from the pinned evaluator, use paired within-category user bootstraps for model differences without changing candidates or evaluator behavior. Such intervals do not correct adaptive validation reuse.

Preserve all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, trial-local artifacts, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with the task default of 200. Diagnostics alone require no predictor modification. Full-catalog diagnostics remain supplementary to pinned sampled HR@10. Twenty qualitative training users provide case evidence only. Keep the final held-out evaluation separate and unavailable during search.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        was_training = self.view.model.training
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with no_grad():
                retain_existing_embedding_and_margin_probes(train_loader)
                for user, prefix in frozen_training_prefix_sample(seed=42, limit=32):
                    candidates = catalog_minus_original_observed_history(user)
                    baseline = score_in_chunks(prefix, candidates)
                    groups = frozen_recent_recurrent_partition(prefix)
                    for contrast in predefined_contrasts(groups):
                        target, controls = exact_matched_subsets(
                            contrast, max_removed=2, repeats=5, seed=42)
                        if controls_are_infeasible(target, controls):
                            record_unavailable_with_reason(contrast)
                            continue
                        for operation in verified_supported_operations():
                            target_scores = score_in_chunks(operation(prefix, target), candidates)
                            control_scores = [
                                score_in_chunks(operation(prefix, subset), candidates)
                                for subset in controls]
                            record_rank_changes_and_control_adjusted_differences(
                                baseline, target_scores, control_scores,
                                tie_break='item_id')
                    record_last_item_fixed_shuffle_control(prefix, candidates)
                    stop_at_predeclared_probe_budget()
                metrics = aggregate_by_user_dataset_and_history_length()
                metrics.update(coverage_runtime_and_user_bootstrap_intervals())
                definitions = metric_formulas_controls_missingness_and_limits()
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(was_training)

# Separate, predefined experiment orchestration:
# 1. Run one budget-matched gated-residual comparator regardless of probe outcome.
# 2. Allow at most one additional probe-nominated experiment under the frozen rule.
# 3. Update predictor writer for any architecture change.
# 4. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10 and log all GPU costs.

originality.positive: Combines recurrence-sensitive controls, explicit matching coverage, SASRec-specific intervention checks, and a budget-matched direct comparator.
originality.negative: Perturbations, conditional matching, and gated pooling are established ingredients; the contribution is a task-specific protocol whose validity remains empirical.

future_potential.positive: Could make diagnostic findings more reproducible across architectures and reveal when diagnostic spending helps model development.
future_potential.negative: No supplied evidence establishes gains over equally tuned direct baselines; sparse matching, redundant signals, and distribution shift can limit usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing encoding and scoring hooks support most computations, and the comparator requires a small architectural addition.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact matching, architecture-aware masking, stable full-catalog scoring, runtime accounting, and predictor synchronization make implementation moderately demanding.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Measures whether the last observed item appears in full-catalog recommendations.
Reports ranking improvements from suppressing the last observed item in evaluated settings.
limitations: Last-item repetition does not isolate recurrence, recency, and popularity.
Filtering gains have limited relevance when the task already excludes observed items.
Does not establish diagnostic cost-effectiveness against a budget-matched gated-history baseline.

related_work.title: Demystifying Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Searches for history changes that alter recommendations using targeted and untargeted counterfactuals.
limitations: Recommendation sensitivity does not establish causal user preference.
Does not establish the proposed position-, time-, and popularity-matched protocol.

related_work.title: RecSys 2025 study of sampled recommendation evaluation
contributions: Examines sampled evaluation through resolution, fidelity, robustness, and predictive power.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned sampled HR@10 objective.
Full-catalog evaluation still observes incomplete interaction-based relevance.

related_work.title: Conditional variable importance for random forests
contributions: Motivates conditional permutation within groups defined by correlated covariates.
limitations: Transfer to sequential history interventions is a proposed adaptation.
Fine conditioning reduces overlap; coarse conditioning leaves residual dependence.
Incremental importance can be small when information is redundant.

related_work.title: Evaluating Feature Importance Estimates
contributions: Introduces ROAR, comparing feature removal after retraining to reduce distribution-shift confounding.
limitations: Evidence comes from a different application domain.
Retraining changes the explained model and consumes additional budget.
The proposed frozen-model probes do not inherit ROAR's retraining control.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation
contributions: Provides concrete absolute-position, padding, causal-attention, and final-position readout semantics relevant to intervention design.
limitations: The actual RecHarness implementation must be checked independently.
Code semantics establish possible intervention confounds, not their empirical magnitude.

related_work.title: SASRec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Illustrates why zeroed states and causal masking alone need not exclude padding keys from attention.
limitations: Repository behavior may change with revisions.
Cannot substitute for inspecting the actual trained architecture's masking and readout behavior.
